estandares: Comprendo y produzco textos cortos sobre rutinas diarias, horarios y hábitos. Pregunto y respondo sobre la frecuencia con la que se realizan actividades cotidianas.
competencias: Preguntar y responder con question words en presente simple; unir ideas con conectores; expresar frecuencia con adverbios y con How often…?; describir la rutina diaria y los hábitos alimenticios.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante construye una línea de tiempo ilustrada de su día, con la hora de cada actividad, un adverbio de frecuencia y un conector en cada oración.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student builds an illustrated timeline of their day, with the time of each activity, a frequency adverb and a connector in every sentence.

lecciones.t_en: Question words with the simple present
lecciones.content_es:
El orden fijo

Wh- + do/does + sujeto + verbo base: What time do you get up?

Cuál usar

  • What time / When – momento: When does the class start?
  • Where – lugar · Who – persona · Why – razón
  • How – modo · What – cosa o actividad

Cuando el Wh- es el sujeto

Si preguntas quién hace la acción, no se usa do/does: Who cooks at home? (no Who does cook).
lecciones.content_en:
The fixed order

Wh- + do/does + subject + base verb: What time do you get up?

Which one to use

  • What time / When – moment: When does the class start?
  • Where – place · Who – person · Why – reason
  • How – manner · What – thing or activity

When the Wh- word is the subject

If you ask who does the action, you do not use do/does: Who cooks at home? (not Who does cook).

fichas.d: Pregunta por la hora exacta de una actividad.
fichas.d_en: Asks for the exact time of an activity.

fichas.d: Orden obligatorio de la pregunta en presente simple.
fichas.d_en: Compulsory word order for simple present questions.

fichas.d: Si el Wh- es el sujeto, no se usa do/does.
fichas.d_en: If the Wh- word is the subject, do/does is not used.

fichas.d: Why pregunta la razón; se responde con because.
fichas.d_en: Why asks for a reason; you answer with because.

quiz.why: La respuesta es una hora, así que se pregunta con What time.
quiz.why_en: The answer is a time, so we ask with What time.

quiz.why: Who es el sujeto de la oración: el verbo va directo y con -s.
quiz.why_en: Who is the subject: the verb goes directly and takes -s.

quiz.q: «___ do you study at night?» — «Because I work in the morning.»
quiz.q_en: "___ do you study at night?" — "Because I work in the morning."
quiz.why: La respuesta empieza con because: la pregunta era por la razón.
quiz.why_en: The answer starts with because: the question asked for a reason.

lecciones.t: Conectores: and, but, or, because, so
lecciones.t_en: Connectors: and, but, or, because, so
lecciones.content_es:
Para qué sirven

Unen ideas y hacen que el texto suene natural en vez de cortado.

  • and – suma: I get up and I take a shower.
  • but – contraste: I like Math but I don't like tests.
  • or – opción: Do you drink milk or juice?
  • because – causa: I'm tired because I study a lot.
  • so – consecuencia: I'm tired, so I go to bed early.

Ojo con because y so

because introduce la causa; so introduce el resultado. Son opuestos: It rains, so I stay home = I stay home because it rains.
lecciones.content_en:
What they are for

They join ideas and make a text sound natural instead of chopped up.

  • and – addition: I get up and I take a shower.
  • but – contrast: I like Math but I don't like tests.
  • or – choice: Do you drink milk or juice?
  • because – cause: I'm tired because I study a lot.
  • so – consequence: I'm tired, so I go to bed early.

Careful with because and so

because introduces the cause; so introduces the result. They are opposites: It rains, so I stay home = I stay home because it rains.

fichas.d: Suma ideas del mismo tipo.
fichas.d_en: Adds ideas of the same kind.

fichas.d: Marca contraste u oposición entre dos ideas.
fichas.d_en: Marks contrast between two ideas.

fichas.d: Introduce la causa: responde a why.
fichas.d_en: Introduces the cause: it answers why.

fichas.d: Introduce la consecuencia o el resultado.
fichas.d_en: Introduces the consequence or result.

quiz.q: «I want to go out, ___ it's raining.»
quiz.q_en: "I want to go out, ___ it's raining."

quiz.why_en: There is a contrast between wanting to go out and the rain: but.

quiz.q_en: "She studies at night ___ she works in the day."

quiz.why_en: The second part is the cause of the first: because.

quiz.q_en: "It's very late, ___ I go to bed."
quiz.why: Irse a la cama es la consecuencia: so.
quiz.why_en: Going to bed is the consequence: so.

lecciones.content_es:
La escala

always (100%) → usually → often → sometimes → rarely / seldom → never (0%).

Dónde se colocan

  • Antes del verbo principal: I always have breakfast.
  • Después del verbo to be: She is never late.
  • Entre auxiliar y verbo: I don't usually go out on Mondays.

Regla importante

never ya es negativo: no se combina con don't. Se dice I never eat fish, no I don't never eat fish.
lecciones.content_en:
The scale

always (100%) → usually → often → sometimes → rarely / seldom → never (0%).

Where they go

  • Before the main verb: I always have breakfast.
  • After the verb to be: She is never late.
  • Between auxiliary and verb: I don't usually go out on Mondays.

Important rule

never is already negative: it is not combined with don't. Say I never eat fish, not I don't never eat fish.

fichas.d: Los extremos de la escala: siempre y nunca.
fichas.d_en: The two ends of the scale: 100% and 0%.

fichas.d: I usually walk to school.
fichas.d_en: I usually walk to school.

fichas.d: He is always happy, no He always is happy.
fichas.d_en: He is always happy, not He always is happy.

fichas.d: No se usa junto con don't o doesn't.
fichas.d_en: It is not used together with don't or doesn't.

quiz.why: Con to be el adverbio va después del verbo.
quiz.why_en: With to be the adverb goes after the verb.

quiz.why: Ser vegetariana implica frecuencia cero: never.
quiz.why_en: Being vegetarian implies zero frequency: never.

quiz.q: ¿Dónde va «often» en «I go to the park»?
quiz.q_en: Where does "often" go in "I go to the park"?

I go often to the park
I often go to the park
I go to the park often it
o_en: Often I go to the park
I go often to the park

quiz.why: El adverbio de frecuencia va antes del verbo principal.
quiz.why_en: The frequency adverb goes before the main verb.

lecciones.t: How often…? y expresiones de frecuencia
lecciones.content_es:
La pregunta

How often do you play soccer? — pide la frecuencia de una actividad.

Las respuestas

  • Con adverbio: I usually play on Saturdays.
  • Con expresión de frecuencia: once a week (una vez por semana), twice a month (dos veces al mes), three times a year, every day, every other day (día por medio).

Cuidado

Una vez es once y dos veces es twice; de tres en adelante se usa times: four times a week.
lecciones.content_en:
The question

How often do you play soccer? — it asks how frequently something happens.

The answers

  • With an adverb: I usually play on Saturdays.
  • With a frequency expression: once a week, twice a month, three times a year, every day, every other day.

Careful

One time is once and two times is twice; from three on you use times: four times a week.

fichas.d: ¿Con qué frecuencia? Pregunta por la periodicidad.
fichas.d_en: Asks how frequently something happens.

fichas.d: Una vez y dos veces. No se dice one time ni two times.
fichas.d_en: One time and two times, in their proper forms.

fichas.d: De tres en adelante se usa times.
fichas.d_en: From three on you use times.

fichas.d: Día por medio: un día sí y otro no.
fichas.d_en: Every second day.

quiz.why: Se pregunta por la frecuencia: How often.
quiz.why_en: We are asking about frequency: How often.

quiz.q: Dos veces por semana se dice…
quiz.q_en: Two times a week is said…
quiz.why: Para dos veces se usa twice.
quiz.why_en: For two times we use twice.

quiz.q: «I go to the gym ___ times a week.»
quiz.q_en: "I go to the gym ___ times a week."
quiz.why: Times solo se usa a partir de tres: three times a week.
quiz.why_en: Times is only used from three on: three times a week.

lecciones.content_es:
Después del verbo

Reemplazan al complemento, no al sujeto: I know her.

Las parejas

  • I → me · you → you · he → him
  • she → her · it → it
  • we → us · they → them

Dónde aparecen

Después del verbo (Call me tonight) o después de una preposición (This gift is for you).

Error frecuente: He helps I → lo correcto es He helps me.
lecciones.content_en:
After the verb

They replace the object, not the subject: I know her.

The pairs

  • I → me · you → you · he → him
  • she → her · it → it
  • we → us · they → them

Where they appear

After the verb (Call me tonight) or after a preposition (This gift is for you).

Common mistake: He helps I → the correct form is He helps me.

fichas.d_en: Object pronouns of I, he and she.

fichas.d: Pronombres objeto de we y they.
fichas.d_en: Object pronouns of we and they.

fichas.d_en: with me, for you, about them.

fichas.d_en: her works as object (I see her) and possessive (her book).

quiz.why: Después del verbo se usa el pronombre objeto me.
quiz.why_en: After the verb we use the object pronoun me.

quiz.why: They como complemento se convierte en them.
quiz.why_en: They as an object becomes them.

quiz.why: Después de una preposición va el pronombre objeto him.
quiz.why_en: After a preposition we use the object pronoun him.

lecciones.content_es:
Preguntar la hora

What time is it? — It's seven o'clock.

Las formas

  • En punto: o'clock — It's three o'clock.
  • Y cuarto: quarter past — It's quarter past four (4:15).
  • Y media: half past — It's half past six (6:30).
  • Menos cuarto: quarter to — It's quarter to nine (8:45).
  • Minutos sueltos: ten past five (5:10), twenty to eight (7:40).

Forma digital

También se puede leer el número tal cual: It's seven fifteen. Y se usa a.m. (mañana) y p.m. (tarde y noche).
lecciones.content_en:
Asking the time

What time is it? — It's seven o'clock.

The forms

  • On the hour: o'clock — It's three o'clock.
  • Quarter past: It's quarter past four (4:15).
  • Half past: It's half past six (6:30).
  • Quarter to: It's quarter to nine (8:45).
  • Other minutes: ten past five (5:10), twenty to eight (7:40).

Digital form

You can also read the numbers directly: It's seven fifteen. And we use a.m. and p.m.

fichas.d: Se usa solo con horas exactas: five o'clock.
fichas.d_en: Used only for exact hours: five o'clock.

fichas.d: Y media: half past six son las 6:30.
fichas.d_en: Half past six means 6:30.

fichas.d: Menos cuarto: quarter to nine son las 8:45.
fichas.d_en: Quarter to nine means 8:45.

fichas.d: past hasta el minuto 30; to después del 30.
fichas.d_en: past up to minute 30; to after minute 30.

fichas.d: Antes y después del mediodía.
fichas.d_en: Before and after noon.

quiz.why: La media hora pasada se dice half past + la hora.
quiz.why_en: Half an hour after is said half past + the hour.

quiz.why: Quarter to five son quince minutos antes de las cinco: 4:45.
quiz.why_en: Quarter to five is fifteen minutes before five: 4:45.

quiz.why: O'clock solo acompaña horas en punto, sin minutos.
quiz.why_en: O'clock only goes with exact hours, with no minutes.

lecciones.content_es:
Verbos de la rutina

get up – levantarse · take a shower – ducharse · brush my teeth – cepillarse los dientes · get dressed – vestirse · have breakfast / lunch / dinner · go to school · do homework · go to bed – acostarse.

Cómo se cuenta un día

I get up at 6:00. Then I take a shower and I have breakfast. I go to school at 7:00. In the afternoon I do my homework, and at 9:30 I go to bed.

Palabras de secuencia

first, then, after that, finally.
lecciones.content_en:
Routine verbs

get up · take a shower · brush my teeth · get dressed · have breakfast / lunch / dinner · go to school · do homework · go to bed.

How to tell your day

I get up at 6:00. Then I take a shower and I have breakfast. I go to school at 7:00. In the afternoon I do my homework, and at 9:30 I go to bed.

Sequence words

first, then, after that, finally.

fichas.d: Levantarse de la cama. Diferente de wake up (despertarse).
fichas.d_en: To get out of bed. Different from wake up.

fichas.d: Desayunar. Se usa have, no eat.
fichas.d_en: To eat the morning meal: we use have.

fichas.d: Hacer tareas: la colocación correcta es do, no make.
fichas.d_en: The correct collocation is do homework, not make.

fichas.d: Palabras para ordenar la secuencia del día.
fichas.d_en: Words used to order the sequence of the day.

quiz.why: Get up significa levantarse de la cama.
quiz.why_en: Get up means to get out of bed.

quiz.why: En inglés la tarea se hace con do, no con make.
quiz.why_en: In English homework goes with do, not make.

quiz.q: «___ I have breakfast, and ___ I go to school.»
quiz.q_en: "___ I have breakfast, and ___ I go to school."
quiz.why: First abre la secuencia y then la continúa.
quiz.why_en: First opens the sequence and then continues it.

lecciones.content_es:
Hábitos buenos y malos

good habits: exercise, drink water, sleep eight hours, eat vegetables, read every day, help at home.
bad habits: skip breakfast, spend hours on the phone, go to bed late, eat too much junk food.

Cómo hablar de ellos

I always drink water, but I sometimes go to bed late.

Para aconsejar se usa should: You should sleep more. · You shouldn't skip breakfast.
lecciones.content_en:
Good and bad habits

good habits: exercise, drink water, sleep eight hours, eat vegetables, read every day, help at home.
bad habits: skip breakfast, spend hours on the phone, go to bed late, eat too much junk food.

How to talk about them

I always drink water, but I sometimes go to bed late.

To give advice we use should: You should sleep more. · You shouldn't skip breakfast.

fichas.d: Hábito: algo que se hace de forma repetida.
fichas.d_en: Something you do repeatedly.

fichas.d: Saltarse el desayuno.
fichas.d_en: To miss the morning meal.

fichas.d: Consejo: deberías / no deberías. El verbo va en base.
fichas.d_en: Advice: the verb after it stays in base form.

fichas.d: Comida chatarra, poco saludable.
fichas.d_en: Unhealthy food.

quiz.why_en: Skipping breakfast is not healthy.

quiz.why_en: The negative of should is shouldn't, with no do auxiliary.

lecciones.content_es:
Las comidas del día

breakfast (desayuno), lunch (almuerzo), snack (refrigerio), dinner (cena).

Frases útiles en la mesa

  • What's for lunch? — ¿Qué hay de almuerzo?
  • I'm hungry / I'm thirsty.
  • Can I have some rice, please?
  • It's delicious! / I don't like it very much.

Ojo

Se dice have lunch, no take lunch. Y I'm hungry (tengo hambre) se construye con to be, no con have.
lecciones.content_en:
Meals of the day

breakfast, lunch, snack, dinner.

Useful phrases at the table

  • What's for lunch?
  • I'm hungry / I'm thirsty.
  • Can I have some rice, please?
  • It's delicious! / I don't like it very much.

Careful

We say have lunch, not take lunch. And I'm hungry uses to be, not have.

fichas.d: Almorzar. Nunca take lunch.
fichas.d_en: To eat the midday meal. Never take lunch.

fichas.d: Tengo hambre: se usa to be, no have.
fichas.d_en: It uses to be, not have.

fichas.d: Refrigerio o merienda entre comidas.
fichas.d_en: A small meal between main meals.

fichas.d: Fórmula educada para pedir algo en la mesa.
fichas.d_en: Polite formula to ask for something at the table.

quiz.why: La colocación correcta es have lunch.
quiz.why_en: The correct collocation is have lunch.

quiz.q_en: How do you say you need something to drink?

quiz.why_en: It uses to be + adjective: I'm thirsty.

quiz.q: ¿Cuál es la comida de la noche?
quiz.why: Dinner es la comida principal de la noche.
quiz.why_en: Dinner is the main evening meal.

lecciones.content_es:
Comida

rice, chicken, beef, fish, eggs, bread, cheese, soup, salad, potatoes, beans.
fruit: apple, banana, orange, strawberry, mango.
vegetables: carrot, tomato, onion, lettuce.

Bebidas

water, milk, juice, coffee, tea, soda, hot chocolate.

Contables e incontables

Se puede contar: two apples, three eggs. No se puede contar: rice, water, milk, bread → se dice some rice, a glass of water, a piece of bread.
lecciones.content_en:
Food

rice, chicken, beef, fish, eggs, bread, cheese, soup, salad, potatoes, beans.
fruit: apple, banana, orange, strawberry, mango.
vegetables: carrot, tomato, onion, lettuce.

Drinks

water, milk, juice, coffee, tea, soda, hot chocolate.

Countable and uncountable

Countable: two apples, three eggs. Uncountable: rice, water, milk, bread → we say some rice, a glass of water, a piece of bread.

fichas.d_en: rice, water, milk, bread: they take no direct number.

fichas.d: Los incontables se miden con recipientes o porciones.
fichas.d_en: Uncountables are measured with containers or portions.

fichas.d: Verduras y frutas. Fruit suele ser incontable.
fichas.d_en: Fruit is usually uncountable in English.

fichas.d_en: some rice, some milk: an indefinite amount.

quiz.why_en: Rice is not counted in units: we say some rice.

quiz.why_en: Water is uncountable and takes some in a request.

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Todo el periodo gira alrededor de contar tu día: a qué hora, con qué frecuencia y por qué. Las preguntas se arman con Wh- + do/does + sujeto + verbo, y las respuestas se unen con conectores.

Puntos gramaticales

  • Adverbios de frecuencia: antes del verbo principal, después de to be.
  • How often…? se responde con once / twice / three times a week.
  • Pronombres objeto: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
  • Conectores: and, but, or, because (causa), so (consecuencia).

Vocabulario

La hora (o'clock, half past, quarter to), rutinas diarias, hábitos buenos y malos, comidas y bebidas contables e incontables.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The whole term is about telling your day: at what time, how often and why. Questions are built with Wh- + do/does + subject + verb, and answers are joined with connectors.

Grammar points

  • Frequency adverbs: before the main verb, after to be.
  • How often…? is answered with once / twice / three times a week.
  • Object pronouns: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
  • Connectors: and, but, or, because (cause), so (consequence).

Vocabulary

Telling the time (o'clock, half past, quarter to), daily routines, good and bad habits, countable and uncountable food and drinks.

never is already negative: it is not combined with don't.

once, twice, and from three on, times.

past up to minute 30; to after minute 30.

Uncountables: some rice, a glass of water.
